case_name: Ram Swaroop And Others v State Of Rajasthan
respondent:
State Of Rajasthan
Supreme Court of India

15 March 2004
Appeal (crl.) 870 of 1997
The Judgment was delivered by : B. P. Singh, J.
1.  In this appeal by special leave the appellants are Ram Swaroop and his two sons Ram Kalyan and Hiralal. They alongwith two
facts: The appellants, Ram Swaroop and his two sons, were tried by the Additional District & Sessions Judge, Bundi, in Sessions Case No. 55 of 1986 charged variously of offences under Sections 302, 302/34 and 323 IPC.
A First Information Report was lodged by Madan Lal (PW-8), son of the deceased, at 8:45 a.m. at P.S. Sadar, Bundi.
The occurrence in question is alleged to have taken place at about 6:00 a.m. on June 6th, 1986.
The houses of Ram Swaroop and Bhanwarlal are adjacent to each other.

Several witnesses were examined by the prosecution in support of its case and out of them, the alleged eye witnesses were Chandra Dutt (PW-3), Gopal (PW-7), Madan Lal (PW-8), Ram Kanwari (PW-9), Kishore (PW-10), Mohan Lal (PW-12), and Nanda (PW-13).
issues: Whether the prosecution had failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
Whether the trial court's acquittal of the appellants was correct.
court_reasoning: The members of the prosecution party and the defence party belong to the same family, the deceased being the brother of appellant No.1, Ram Swaroop while appellant Nos. 2 and 3 are the sons of Ram Swaroop.
PWs. 3, 7, 10 & 12 were declared hostile by the prosecution.
The evidence of this witness discloses they were the only eye witnesses to the occurrence.
This witness was declared hostile and was cross-examined at length by reference to the earlier statement made by him in the course of investigation.
holding: The trial court acquitted them of all the charges levelled against them.

On appeal, the High Court affirmed the acquittal of the two female accused, but while acquitting the appellants of the offence punishable under Section 302 IPC convicted them under Section 304 Part II and Section 323 IPC.
